cases.case_text: A 58-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and bilateral lower-extremity edema over three weeks. Chest radiograph on admission showed cardiomegaly with an enlarged cardiac silhouette and mild pulmonary vascular congestion. Electrocardiogram demonstrated sinus tachycardia with left ventricular hypertrophy criteria. Transthoracic echocardiography confirmed reduced left ventricular ejection fraction consistent with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

A 64-year-old man with a history of hypertension presented to the emergency department with crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm. Electrocardiogram revealed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. Emergent coronary angiography demonstrated a proximal left anterior descending artery occlusion, and the patient underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement.
cases.keywords: myocardial infarction, coronary occlusion, percutaneous intervention

cases.case_text: A 71-year-old woman was referred for evaluation of a new systolic murmur discovered on routine examination. She reported mild fatigue but denied syncope or chest pain. Echocardiography identified severe calcific aortic stenosis with a markedly reduced valve area. A follow-up chest radiograph showed a boot-shaped cardiac silhouette with post-stenotic dilation of the ascending aorta.
cases.keywords: aortic stenosis, valvular heart disease, murmur

cases.case_text: A 45-year-old man presented with palpitations and lightheadedness lasting several hours. Electrocardiogram on presentation showed a narrow-complex tachycardia at 180 beats per minute, consistent with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia. The rhythm terminated after vagal maneuvers, and a subsequent electrocardiogram in sinus rhythm was unremarkable.

A 39-year-old woman in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with new-onset dyspnea and orthopnea. Echocardiography revealed a markedly reduced ejection fraction with global hypokinesis and no prior history of cardiac disease, raising concern for peripartum cardiomyopathy. Chest radiograph showed mild cardiomegaly without frank pulmonary edema.
